management.value: Management/Board: Christian Klein is the CEO and Chairman of SAP's Executive Board. •Klein started working for SAP as a 15-year-old student, literally carrying heavy CRT monitors around the building as part of a school-based internship, and became sole CEO in 2020 at only 39 years of age. •He holds a diploma in International Business Administration from the Baden-Württemberg Cooperative State University (DHBW) in Mannheim, Germany, an institution known for its dual education system that combines academic study with practical work experience in partner companies. SAP was his partner company throughout his studies. •Klein held various positions across SAP including CFO of SAP SuccessFactors (2011–2012), Chief Controlling Officer (2014), and Chief Operating Officer (2016). He joined the Executive Board in 2018 as head of the Intelligent Enterprise Group, responsible for the development and delivery of SAP's core applications including S/4HANA and the Digital Supply Chain portfolio. •On October 11, 2019, he was named Co-CEO alongside Jennifer Morgan, before being appointed sole CEO on April 20, 2020, after Morgan departed in the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic. In May 2025, SAP's Supervisory Board extended Klein's contract to five years, running through April 2030, citing his instrumental role in the company's transformation journey. •Klein is credited with engineering the cloud transition, the single most important strategic shift in SAP's modern history, and delivering on the financial targets he set. In January 2024, he launched a company-wide restructuring program to enhance scalability and drive AI-focused efficiencies, setting targets of ~€10B non-IFRS operating profit and ~€8B free cash flow for 2025, both of which SAP hit.

basis.claim: SAP's pack carries substantive documented fundamentals: 2025 revenue of EUR36,800m with operating margin improving to 26.1% and free cash flow nearly doubling to EUR8.24bn.
